text:
alex_g: quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on the canary after the kernel selector change. continuous-batcher p95 +40ms, and KV miss rate spiked for a subset of long-prefix requests. dumping details here so we can brainstorm early-shed/admit ideas.

maria_k: copying profiler output would help. is this consistently reproducible on the same trace or noisy?

alex_g: consistent on the canary shard (5% traffic). sample traces attached to the perf job — main delta is kernel switch that increased per-token microcost for short tails when KV misses happen. also noticed queue depth oscillations.

prashant: can you paste the flamegraph link? curious if the stall is in memory copy or a new kernel path.

alex_g: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/canary/1977771234
flame shows extra memcpy + kernel-launch overhead right after KV lookup miss path (we're doing a small fallback decode kernel).

jen: maybe we should bias admit toward KV-hit requests first so the batch is "KV-friendly". if a batch is > 25% misses, we could do early-shed of small prefixes or tighten token budget to favor latency.

sam: idea: per-queue token_budget_target + kv_miss_threshold that triggers a softer admission policy (emit 429-soft or enqueue-to-burst for next window).

prashant: +1. also consider kernel-hinting: annotate requests with expected kv_hit probability (from cache stats) and let batcher prefer high-prob items when forming the batch. That helps kernel selection and reduces mixed-kernel batches.

alex_g: sketched config for experiment:
```json
{
  "queue_admit": "kv_priority_soft",
  "token_budget_target": 256,
  "early_shed_small_prefix_ms": 10,
  "kv_miss_threshold_pct": 15,
  "mixed_kernel_penalty_ms": 20
}
```
This would: prefer KV-hits in batch formation, if miss fraction >15% do early-shed of tiny prefixes (<3 tokens) and lower token budget to keep latency SLOs. Mixed-kernel penalty injects a small artificial cost to discourage mixing.

maria_k: how do we surface "early-shed" behavior to caller? we should be doing soft 429s with Retry-After and telemetry to detect user-impact. If we hard drop, apps see errors.

alex_g: plan is soft 429 (x-early-shed: true) so clients can retry quickly. we can also mark route-level metrics: shed_count, shed_latency_saved, shed_kv_miss_pct.

sam: metric set I'd want in A/B: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_hit_rate_by_route, mixed_kernel_batch_pct, soft_429_rate, overall throughput, and any downstream error spikes.

prashant: quick sanity check script folks can run:
```
# fetch recent canary traces and compute kv-miss rate per batch
curl -s "https://perf.redwood/api/canary/1977771234/traces" | jq '.traces[] | {batch_id, kv_miss_rate, tokens, latency_ms}' | head
```

jen: two experiment arms proposed: (A) kv-priority-soft on 5% traffic, (B) kv-priority-soft + early-shed on 5% (diff in policy only). compare for 72h. roll back on any >3% p95 regression or >0.5% increase in error rate.

alex_g: agree. I'll push a canary config and start collects. infra-bot will create the experiment and dashboards.

infra-bot: created experiment "kv-priority-early-shed" id=exp-20260317-1 arms=[A:5%,B:5%] dashboards=/dash/exp-20260317-1 metrics=[p95_latency,kv_hit_rate,mixed_kernel_pct,soft_429_rate]

maria_k: small nit — make sure the rollout has a per-route opt-out and does not touch enterprise-customer routes. put it behind the perf-experiments flag.

alex_g: done. exclusion list added. config pushed to staging. testing trace collector now.

sam: one more thought — for long-sequence requests, token_budget_target shouldn't be a single global number. maybe target = min(1024, max(128, median_seq_len * 2)). that prevents small-budget thrash for long jobs.

prashant: agreed. also instrument per-kernel latency distribution so we can detect if the mixed batches are causing tail amplification.

jen: ok let's reconvene after 24h of data. if early-shed reduces p95 by >20ms without increasing error rate, we can consider scaling to 20% traffic. :thumbsup:

alex_g: thanks all — will post initial perf dump in ~24h. cc @maria_k for dashboards and @sam to watch SLO alerts.

sam: good plan. ping me if infra-bot alerts. :pray:

infra-bot: alert subscription created: exp-20260317-1 -> slack#eng-runtime (p95>baseline+20ms or soft_429_rate>0.5%)

alex_g: initial 12h snapshot: p95 down ~8ms in arm B, kv_hit_rate up 3% on prioritized routes, soft_429 rose 0.12% (within expectations). full 24h tomorrow.

maria_k: nice. attaching AB plot to dashboard.

jen: great signals — thanks for running it.

prashant: if this looks good at 24h, we should iterate on mixed_kernel_penalty tuning next (start at 10ms, go to 30ms).

alex_g: noted. locking this thread. will reopen if we see regressions or new ideas.
